transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just keep getting up when I'm really supposed to stay put. Like, during client interviews. I'm a private investigator, mostly corporate stuff, some infidelity—which honestly is just so depressing. Just last week I had this woman in my office going on and on about her husband's offshore accounts, and I just could not stay in my chair. I kept popping up, pacing to the window, checking the blinds. Which I guess is a habit anyway in my line of work, you always want to check your sightlines, but still. 

And it happens during tutoring sessions too. I tutor on the side, mostly history. History is fascinating, especially the Gilded Age, there's so much corruption that totally mirrors today's local politics if you really look at the zoning board records. But anyway, I'm up and down the whole time I'm trying to teach. 

Even at my book club! We're reading that new thriller everyone is talking about, the one with the unreliable narrator on the boat? It's okay, a bit derivative of Gone Girl if you ask me, but the host made these amazing little cucumber sandwiches. But yeah, the point is, people are really starting to notice. They look at me like, why can't she just sit and listen for five minutes? And I don't really have a good answer for them.
Have you had a period of several days when your mood was unusually high or irritable?

Unusually high or irritable? No, I don't think so. I mean, I get annoyed, sure. Like when I'm doing surveillance and the guy I'm tailing goes into a restaurant with only one exit and I have to sit in my car for three hours. That is incredibly irritating. Especially if it's hot out. I had this one case last summer, middle of July, tracking this mid-level executive who was supposedly on medical leave but was actually playing golf every day. The heat in that car was unbelievable. I tried bringing one of those little battery-powered fans, but it just blew hot air around. And the batteries died after like an hour anyway. Have you noticed how expensive D batteries are getting? It's ridiculous. I ended up buying rechargeable ones, but then I always forget to actually charge them, which kind of defeats the purpose. But anyway, no, not like a whole period of days where my mood is weirdly high or anything. Just normal stuff.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention when you need to focus on something?

Trouble sustaining attention? Honestly, no, I wouldn't say that. When I need to focus, I focus. Like, if I'm going through financial records for a case, I can sit there and look for the discrepancies. It's actually kind of like a puzzle, you know? Like Sudoku, but with someone's hidden assets. I used to do a ton of Sudoku. I had this app on my phone, but then they updated it and changed the interface, and it just wasn't the same. The colors were all garish—bright neon green and purple. Who wants to look at that when they're trying to concentrate? It gave me a headache. I tried switching to crosswords, the Sunday Times ones, but they get so obscure. Like, a five-letter word for a 14th-century Mongolian coin? How is anyone supposed to know that without looking it up? And if you look it up, it feels like cheating. My brother says it's not cheating, it's 'research,' but he's a lawyer, so he has a way of twisting words. He actually just bought a new house, a mid-century modern, beautiful lines, but the roof needs a complete tear-off. But yeah, to answer your question, no, I don't really have trouble paying attention to things.
When you were a child, were you often unable to stay seated or were you very physically restless compared with other kids?

Oh, as a kid? Yeah, definitely. My grade-school report cards were basically just a broken record. They always said I was bright, but I couldn't stay in my seat or wait my turn. My mother still jokes about it. She says I treated every classroom like a crime scene I had to pace through to investigate. Which is funny, considering what I do now, right? I guess the signs were all there. 

Speaking of my mom, she just retired and moved to Florida. Classic, I know. But she didn't go to Miami or anything, she went to this little town on the Gulf Coast. The beaches there are gorgeous, but the humidity is just out of control. I went down to visit her last month and my hair was just a frizz ball the entire time. I tried every anti-frizz serum I could find at the drugstore down there, but nothing worked. I ended up just wearing a baseball cap the whole trip. It was a vintage Mets hat I found at a thrift store. I love thrift stores, you never know what you're going to find. Last week I found this amazing mid-century lamp, brass, completely tarnished, but I spent all Sunday polishing it and now it looks brand new. I had to buy special polish for it, the kind that smells awful, like ammonia and old pennies. But yeah, to answer your question, I was always up and moving around as a kid, for sure.
Do you often interrupt people before they finish speaking?

Oh, interrupting? Yeah, I do that. A lot, actually. Like, if I'm at the precinct or something and I hear the junior detectives discussing a lead, or even just a neighbor talking in the hallway of my building, I just... jump right in. I start firing off questions or giving them advice before they've even asked for it. And then afterward, I'm like, 'Wow, I totally just barged into a conversation that had nothing to do with me.' 

It's just, when I hear people trying to figure something out, my brain automatically starts trying to solve it for them. It's like a reflex. Speaking of reflexes, I went to the doctor for a physical last week, just a routine thing, and he did that little hammer tap on the knee? My leg kicked up so high I almost kicked his clipboard out of his hands. I felt terrible. He laughed it off, but still. He had this really nice pen, too, one of those heavy metal ones that writes super smooth. I meant to ask him what brand it was, but I got distracted because they had this poster on the wall about Lyme disease, and the tick on it was magnified like a thousand times. It was horrifying. Have you ever seen one up close? They look like little aliens. I had a case once where I had to do surveillance in this heavily wooded area up in Westchester, and I was so paranoid about ticks I practically bathed in bug spray. The smell was awful, like citronella and chemicals. It lingered in my car for weeks. I tried everything to get it out—baking soda, coffee grounds, leaving the windows down. Nothing worked. I finally had to get it professionally detailed. But yeah, interrupting people, that's definitely something I do. I just can't seem to stop myself sometimes.
